To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) aggregating several CPU cores in a context allows us to execute larger parallel kernels and thus to better exploit the parallelism of accelerator based machines; (2) our solution is able to handle the interaction between the task and the OpenMP based scheduling strategies; (3) our solution outperformed state of the art solutions on a platform equipped by 20 CPU cores, 4 GPU devices and a peak performance of up to 4.5TFlop/s.
we show how to efficiently exploit two levels of parallelism on modern accelerator based machines by relying on the task parallelism and the task granularity.

1) the use of task based runtimes for heterogeneous computing is a promising approach to exploit the parallelism of complex platforms and 2) the use of scheduling contexts is a powerful tool to exploit the two level parallelism of task based applications over heterogeneous machines.
In summary, our research is concerned with

exploiting the two level parallelism of modern computing platforms and our solution relies on the aggregation of computing resources at the granularity of the parallel tasks in order to achieve better performance.

we show how we can use the task based programming model to exploit two-level parallelism on heterogeneous architectures by using scheduling contexts and aggregating computing resources.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the task granularity problem is still relevant and needs to be tackled to reach the best performance on modern accelerator based machines.
it is possible to exploit the two level parallelism of modern machines by delegating the management of the parallelism to the runtime systems.
the use of scheduling contexts allows us to exploit the two level parallelism of the application at hand, i.e., the parallelism at task level and the parallelism at CPU level.
